solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Curlers having clothing with name written inside

indicators.note: something written inside is set within the outer word, so one piece sits in another

blocks.note: togs is informal British for clothes
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone's hair curlers come with a garment that has a name tag inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Curlers here are not people or rollers but the heated tool; N goes inside TOGS to give TONGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Curling tongs are the heated metal implement used for putting waves into hair.

clue.text: Drumming is beginning to threaten — you’ll see me turning to hide

definitions.text: you’ll see me turning to hide

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a tattoo is a rhythmic drumbeat, as in a military tattoo
taken as written
first letter of threaten

explanation.surface: A menacing drumbeat starts up, and someone watching turns away to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: hide means skin, and the speaker is someone who turns to your skin to work on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who inks designs into customers' skin turns their attention and needle to that hide.

clue.text: Number getting endless home service

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A performer's act involves a house-to-house service that never quite finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Number looks like a figure but is the abbreviation NO; NEST loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the monastic day of prayer, the office said at the ninth hour, mid-afternoon, is called by this name.

clue.text: Father will collar United over match official for certain

indicators.note: in a down entry, being over something means sitting above it, so this comes first
to collar someone is to grab them round the neck, so one piece encloses the rest

blocks.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
short for referee

explanation.surface: A dad vows to grab Manchester United's players before they confront the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means above, so United's letter sits on top of the official, and the father's name opens after its first letter to hold both.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bound to succeed is guaranteed, so the adjective matches a phrase meaning certain.

clue.text: System of rules suppressing rebellious nonsense leads to uprising

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down, so one piece is kept within another

blocks.note: a code is a set of rules
up in arms, rising against authority
tat is British slang for tasteless rubbish

explanation.surface: A rulebook meant to stamp out rebel talk only provokes revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Rebellious gives UP, as in 'the people are up'; tat, British for cheap junk, stretches to nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden seizure of government power by a small group is a kind of revolt against rulers.

clue.text: Mock opera’s ultimate conclusion

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the final one, so only that is kept

blocks.note: cod is British slang for fake or parody, as in cod Latin
last letter of opera

explanation.surface: A spoof opera reaches its grand finale.
explanation.walkthrough: Mock is an adjective here, not a verb: COD is British slang for sham or imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the closing section added after the main structure is the piece's ending passage.

clue.text: Machine put to work without much impact

indicators.note: setting material to work means handling and reshaping it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A machine is set going but achieves very little.
explanation.walkthrough: Put to work reads as the verb phrase for the machine, but put belongs to the fodder and to work is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking forceful stress or emphasis makes little impression, so it lacks impact.

clue.text: Appropriate seeing change to older coinage in receipt

indicators.note: a change to the older coinage swaps a modern money letter for its pre-decimal equivalent

blocks.note: to pocket something is to take it for yourself
D was the symbol for the old penny before decimalisation; P is the new penny

explanation.surface: An official finds it fitting to note the switch to old money on a receipt.
explanation.walkthrough: Appropriate is a verb, to pocket; in POCKET the new-penny P becomes the old-penny D.
explanation.definitionFit: A docket is a document listing goods delivered or paid for, so it serves as a receipt.

clue.text: Describing glands, look, inside damaged nostril

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece goes into the other
something damaged is broken up, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: la is an old exclamation meaning look or behold
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor examining glands says look at this injured nostril.
explanation.walkthrough: Look is the archaic exclamation 'la', like 'lo', not a verb; it lands between the sixth and seventh letters of the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the tonsils, the pair of lymph glands at the back of the throat.

clue.text: Weight and volume after inclusion of additional unspecified number

indicators.note: once something is included it is taken into the middle, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: tone taken loosely as the level of a sound
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A description of weight and volume measurements that adds in another variable number.
explanation.walkthrough: TONE already has one N; the extra unspecified number is a second N slipped inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of mass equal to a thousand kilograms is used to measure heavy loads.

clue.text: Card game dropping one of its players in quality Home Counties town

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so a letter is removed
in means placed within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: tone is character or quality
bridge is a four-player card game
the four bridge players are North, South, East and West; East is E

explanation.surface: A bridge four loses a player in a smart commuter town near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The player dropped is East, the last letter left over once the game sits inside. The Home Counties are the counties around London; Tonbridge is in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a market town in Kent, one of the counties bordering London known collectively this way.

clue.text: Cathedral dignitary, head of chapter, not giving name?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: first letter of chapter
anonymous, with no name given

explanation.surface: A senior churchman who heads the cathedral chapter refuses to be named.
explanation.walkthrough: Head of chapter sounds like a job title for the dignitary, since canons sit in a cathedral chapter; here it is just the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a clergyman who is a member of a cathedral's governing body, a senior church office.

clue.text: Turn into fossil? Most of fossil badly done, ending in ignominy

indicators.note: most but not all, so the last letter is dropped
something done badly is botched and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of ignominy

explanation.surface: A botched fossil ends in shame for whoever tried to create one.
explanation.walkthrough: FOSSIL minus its last letter is FOSSI, rearranged to OSSIF, then Y is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To harden into bone or stony rigidity is what happens as remains are preserved in rock.

clue.text: Little from Escoffier to fill primate’s hunger

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so one piece is put within another

blocks.note: Escoffier was a French chef, so little in French: petit
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A small morsel from a famous French chef satisfies a monkey's craving.
explanation.walkthrough: Auguste Escoffier was a celebrated French chef, so his word for little is the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: A desire to eat, a craving for food, is exactly what the word means in everyday use.

clue.text: Italian composer in book: iconic in translation that woman penned

indicators.note: a translation turns words into new forms, so these letters are reworked
something penned is shut in an enclosure, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: An Italian composer appears in a book that is a classic in translation, written by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That woman penned' means the pronoun is held inside the reworked letters, which split three and three around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Boccherini was an eighteenth-century Italian cellist and composer, known for his famous minuet.

clue.text: Unsympathetic emperor’s replacing one with offspring

indicators.note: replacing one thing with another swaps a letter out for a new piece

blocks.note: imperial means belonging to an emperor
I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is offspring

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted emperor passes over someone in favour of his own child.
explanation.walkthrough: Emperor's is the possessive adjective IMPERIAL, whose second I is swapped for SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cold and lacking human warmth or feeling towards individuals is showing no sympathy.

clue.text: Continue to publish about church in US university city

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: to print on is to keep publishing
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A publisher keeps putting out work about the church in an American college town.
explanation.walkthrough: The church here is the Church of England, abbreviated in crosswords to its two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton, New Jersey, is home to the Ivy League university of the same name.

clue.text: Remote distance recalled after leaving end of line

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run backwards
the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept
leaving means departing, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: miles measure distance
last letter of line

explanation.surface: A distant place is remembered after someone leaves the end of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: MILES reversed is SELIM; removing the E leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote chance is a slight one, and a slim chance means the same small possibility.

clue.text: Hormone turning in zucchini, not a lemon

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the letters are read backwards
in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the vegetable to the start of the fruit

explanation.surface: A hormone is at work in a courgette rather than in a citrus fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'zucchINI NOT A LEMon' backwards reveals the answer; the vegetable and fruit are only there to carry the letters. Zucchini is the American and Italian name for a courgette.
explanation.definitionFit: Melatonin is a hormone produced by the pineal gland that regulates sleep and waking cycles.

clue.text: A simple golf-shot starts to cause hesitation in a crisis

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
a tap-in is a very short, easy putt
first letters of cause and hesitation

explanation.surface: A golfer freezes over an easy putt when the pressure is on.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf-shot is a tap-in, the short putt knocked into the hole from close range.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means if absolutely necessary, when an emergency leaves no better option.

clue.text: Upset about river excursion

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: to tip over is to upset
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed about a river outing.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset is not a reversal or anagram signal here but a verb meaning to tip, knock over.
explanation.definitionFit: A short journey taken for pleasure, such as a day out, is an outing of this kind.

clue.text: Small particular changes ignoring an area of Biblical studies

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is removed
changes means alterations, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Minor, fussy changes skip over one section of Bible scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: One A is removed from PARTICULAR before the rest is rearranged; S goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the holy writings of the Bible, the adjective describes that field of theology.

clue.text: French person’s conclusion is to accept my old coin

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: fin is French for end
lor is a dated exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: A Frenchman concludes he must take the old coin offered to him.
explanation.walkthrough: My is an exclamation of surprise, not a possessive; 'lor' is a dated cockney form of Lord!
explanation.definitionFit: The florin was a British coin worth two shillings, withdrawn after decimalisation in 1971.

clue.text: Lake expert spinning in Black Sea, unable to progress?

indicators.note: spinning turns something round, so its letters face the other way
in means placed within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
L is the abbreviation for lake
an ace is an expert
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A lake sailing expert spins out of control on the Black Sea and cannot get anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Sea is not the place name: B and MED together hold the reversed LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing ship left motionless by lack of wind cannot move forward; the question mark flags the nautical sense.

clue.text: Upset no key office staff?

indicators.note: upsetting turns something upside down, so in a down entry the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
Tab is a key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: An office has no one to handle the keyboard, and the workers are upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Office staff looks like employees, but it is a staff carried as a symbol of office.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short rod carried as an emblem of authority, like a field marshal's, hence a staff of office.

clue.text: Drunkard throttling glutton delivering tap

indicators.note: throttling means gripping round the throat, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
a pig is a glutton

explanation.surface: A drunk strangles a greedy rival to get at the beer tap.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivering is a link: the wordplay delivers the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a small peg or valve on a cask controlling the flow, so it works as a tap.

clue.text: Mean opening of gallery to have famous gallery upset

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
upsetting turns something over, so in a down entry the letters run backwards

blocks.note: first letter of gallery
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A stingy gallery owner is envious of a famous gallery and upsets it.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean is a verb here, as in 'what are you getting at?', not an adjective for stinginess. The Tate is London's national art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to imply or intend to convey, as when asking what someone is driving at.

clue.text: Degree of freedom in Shakespeare’s work?

blocks.note: first meaning: slack or room to move, as in a rope
second meaning: a drama, the kind of thing Shakespeare wrote

explanation.walkthrough: The first half sounds like an academic term; it means room for movement, the give in a loose part.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both looseness allowing movement in a mechanism and a stage drama written for performance.

clue.text: Teacher rejected backing key component of education? About time

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: something rejected is thrown out
the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A teacher turned down for supporting a core part of schooling asks whether it is about time.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT reversed plus R gives TUOR, which wraps round T. The question mark flags R as one of the three Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: A private instructor or university supervisor who teaches individuals or small groups is a kind of teacher.

clue.text: Part of London — I pass to North

blocks.note: taken as written
to sling is to throw or pass
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A traveller describes heading north through part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Pass means to toss or hand over, so SLING; the rest is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a borough of inner north London, one district of the capital.

clue.text: One new bird observed in US city is a thing of no importance

indicators.note: something observed in a place is seen within it, so these pieces go inside

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a tit is a small bird
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A newly arrived bird spotted in New York turns out to be insignificant.
explanation.walkthrough: The US city is New York, whose two initials split to enclose everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonentity is someone or something with no significance, a person or thing that counts for nothing.

clue.text: Very keen about hard working, engaging leaders of our teams

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so one piece is held inside another
the leaders of words are their first letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
first letters of our and teams
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A coach is very keen on hard work and involves the captains of the teams.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard and working join first; the leaders then go between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being strict or enthusiastic about something, insisting on it, is the idiom's sense.
